correctness.rationale: With \(\alpha=\varepsilon a\) and \(\theta=\varepsilon b\), the exact one-step cumulative hazard is \(d_z=\varepsilon(a+c r^z)\). For fixed \(z\), the PMF therefore satisfies \(p_z=\varepsilon(a+c r^z)+O(\varepsilon^2)\). Substitution into the PMF log-concavity determinant gives the strictly negative coefficient \(-a c r^{z-1}(r-1)^2\). This proves an open small-rate failure region without relying on finite computation. The standalone decimal checker reproduces the explicit admissible counterexample and the normalized asymptotic coefficient.

value.rationale: PMF log-concavity is presented by the target as a foundational structural property supporting unimodality and stability under convolution. The finding does more than provide an isolated numerical counterexample: it proves that for every fixed finite prefix, a whole low-rate regime makes all corresponding PMF curvature determinants negative. This identifies a systematic mechanism behind the failure and pinpoints the invalid survival-to-PMF step in the published proof.
